exercises.title: Should Be Equal - Basic Comparison
exercises.description: Learn the most fundamental assertion: checking if two values are exactly equal.

story.setup: MENTOR-9: "Storing data means nothing if we can't verify it's correct. The Should Be Equal keyword is your primary validation toolâ€”it checks if actual matches expected."
story.context: Assertions are Robot Framework's way of validating that your system behaves correctly. If values don't match, the test fails immediately, alerting you to problems.
story.success: MENTOR-9: "Perfect! The assertion passed because 'Operational' equals 'Operational'. If they hadn't matched, the test would have failed with a clear error message. That's how we catch bugs."

instructions: Create a test case named 'System Status Validation'
Use Should Be Equal to compare ${actual_status} and ${expected_status}
Log a success message: 'Status check passed!'

Arguments must be separated by at least 2 spaces (4 recommended)

The keyword is case-insensitive: should be equal = SHOULD BE EQUAL
First argument is 'actual', second is 'expected' (convention)
exercises.solution:
*** Test Cases ***
System Status Validation
    ${actual_status}      Set Variable    Operational
    ${expected_status}    Set Variable    Operational
    Should Be Equal       ${actual_status}    ${expected_status}

    ${ship_name}          Set Variable    Starlight Explorer
    Should Be Equal       ${ship_name}    Starlight Explorer

theory.title: Exercise 1.3.1: Should Be Equal - The Foundation of Validation
theory.content:
MENTOR-9 brings up two holographic panels side by side, both displaying "OPERATIONAL".

"PROTO-7, storing data is only half the job. We must verify it's correct. The Should Be Equal keyword is your primary validation toolâ€”it compares actual vs expected values."

What Are Assertions?

Assertions are statements that validate expected conditions. If the condition is true, the test continues. If false, the test fails immediately with an error.

Why Assertions Matter

  • Catch bugs early: Test fails when behavior changes unexpectedly
  • Document expectations: Code shows what should happen
  • Prevent regressions: Ensure fixes don't break again
  • Build confidence: Passing tests mean working software

The Should Be Equal Keyword

The most fundamental assertion in Robot Framework:

Should Be Equal    ${actual}    ${expected}

Behavior:

  • âś… If ${actual} == ${expected} â†’ Test continues
  • âťŚ If ${actual} â‰  ${expected} â†’ Test fails with error message

Basic Usage

*** Test Cases ***
Simple Equality Check
    ${status}           Set Variable    Operational
    Should Be Equal     ${status}    Operational
    Log                 Validation passed!

What Happens:

  1. Create variable ${status} with value "Operational"
  2. Compare ${status} to "Operational"
  3. They match â†’ assertion passes â†’ test continues
  4. Log success message

When Assertions Fail

*** Test Cases ***
Failing Assertion Example
    ${status}           Set Variable    Damaged
    Should Be Equal     ${status}    Operational
    # âťŚ TEST FAILS HERE - next line never executes
    Log                 This won't run

Error Message:

AssertionError: Damaged != Operational

The test stops at the failed assertion. Subsequent keywords don't execute.

Comparing Variables

*** Test Cases ***
Compare Two Variables
    ${actual}           Set Variable    Robot Framework
    ${expected}         Set Variable    Robot Framework
    Should Be Equal     ${actual}    ${expected}
    Log                 Both variables match!

String Comparison (Default)

By default, Should Be Equal compares values as strings:

*** Test Cases ***
String Comparison
    ${number_as_string}    Set Variable    42
    Should Be Equal        ${number_as_string}    42      # âś… Works: "42" == "42"
    Should Be Equal        ${number_as_string}    042     # âťŚ Fails: "42" != "042"

Adding Custom Error Messages

You can add a custom message as the third argument:

*** Test Cases ***
Custom Error Message
    ${status}    Set Variable    Damaged
    Should Be Equal    ${status}    Operational    msg=System status check failed! Expected Operational but got ${status}

Error Output:

AssertionError: System status check failed! Expected Operational but got Damaged

Common Use Cases

1. API Response Validation

*** Test Cases ***
API Status Check
    ${response_status}    Set Variable    200
    Should Be Equal       ${response_status}    200    msg=Expected HTTP 200 OK

2. Configuration Verification

*** Test Cases ***
Config Check
    ${env}              Set Variable    production
    ${expected_env}     Set Variable    production
    Should Be Equal     ${env}    ${expected_env}    msg=Environment mismatch!

3. User Input Validation

*** Test Cases ***
Login Check
    ${username}         Set Variable    admin@example.com
    Should Be Equal     ${username}    admin@example.com

Should Be Equal vs Should Be Equal As Strings

KeywordBehaviorWhen to Use
Should Be Equal String comparison (default) Most common cases
Should Be Equal As Strings Explicit string comparison When clarity needed
Should Be Equal As Integers Numeric comparison Comparing numbers: 42 == 042
Should Be Equal As Numbers Float/decimal comparison Comparing 3.14 == 3.140

Case Sensitivity

String comparisons ARE case-sensitive:

*** Test Cases ***
Case Matters
    ${status}           Set Variable    operational
    Should Be Equal     ${status}    Operational    # âťŚ FAILS: "operational" != "Operational"

Use Should Be Equal As Strings with ignore_case=True for case-insensitive:

*** Test Cases ***
Case Insensitive
    ${status}                      Set Variable    operational
    Should Be Equal As Strings     ${status}    Operational    ignore_case=True    # âś… PASSES

Assertion Keyword Flexibility

Like all Robot Framework keywords, assertion keywords are case-insensitive and spacing-flexible:

*** Test Cases ***
Keyword Variations
    ${x}    Set Variable    test
    
    Should Be Equal          ${x}    test    # Standard
    should be equal          ${x}    test    # Lowercase
    SHOULD BE EQUAL          ${x}    test    # Uppercase
    ShouldÂ·Â·BeÂ·Â·Equal        ${x}    test    # Extra spaces
    ShouldBeEqual            ${x}    test    # No spaces
    
    # All are IDENTICAL!

Best Practices

1. Descriptive Variable Names

*** Test Cases ***
Good Practice
    ${actual_status}      Set Variable    OK
    ${expected_status}    Set Variable    OK
    Should Be Equal       ${actual_status}    ${expected_status}
    
    # Clear what's being compared

2. Use Custom Error Messages for Complex Checks

*** Test Cases ***
Clear Errors
    ${user_role}    Set Variable    guest
    Should Be Equal    ${user_role}    admin    msg=User does not have admin privileges (role: ${user_role})

3. One Assertion Per Logical Check

*** Test Cases ***
Multiple Checks
    ${status}    Set Variable    active
    ${role}      Set Variable    admin
    
    Should Be Equal    ${status}    active    msg=Status check failed
    Should Be Equal    ${role}      admin     msg=Role check failed
    
    # Separate assertions = separate failure messages

Common Mistakes

âťŚ Wrong: Comparing without storing

*** Test Cases ***
Wrong Approach
    Should Be Equal    Operational    Operational    # Works but no actual value tested

âś… Right: Store actual value first

*** Test Cases ***
Correct Approach
    ${status}           Set Variable    Operational
    Should Be Equal     ${status}    Operational

MENTOR-9: "Create two variables: one for actual ship status, one for expected. Use Should Be Equal to validate they match. Then verify the ship name. Show me you can catch discrepancies before they become disasters."

exercises.title: Should Contain - Substring Validation
exercises.description: Learn to validate that strings contain specific substrings—essential for error messages and flexible validation.

story.setup: MENTOR-9: "Not all validation needs exact matches. Often you just need to verify a message contains specific text. Should Contain is perfect for this."
story.context: Error messages, status strings, and log outputs often have variable parts. Substring checking lets you validate the important parts while ignoring the rest.
story.success: MENTOR-9: "Perfect! The error message contains 'breach'—that's what matters. Substring validation is more flexible than exact matching."

instructions: Create a test case named 'Error Message Validation'
Create ${error_msg} with value 'Hull breach detected in sector 7'
Use Should Contain to verify ${error_msg} contains 'breach'
Use Should Contain to verify ${error_msg} contains 'sector 7'
Create ${status_report} with value 'System diagnostic: 3 warnings, 1 critical error'
Use Should Contain to verify ${status_report} contains 'critical error'
hints: Should Contain syntax: Should Contain    ${string}    ${substring}
First argument is the full string, second is the substring to find
Substring search IS case-sensitive: 'Breach' ≠ 'breach'
If substring not found, test fails
The keyword is flexible: should contain = SHOULD CONTAIN
Use this for partial matches when exact match isn't needed
exercises.solution:
*** Test Cases ***
Error Message Validation
    ${error_msg}         Set Variable    Hull breach detected in sector 7
    Should Contain       ${error_msg}    breach
    Should Contain       ${error_msg}    sector 7
    Log                  Error message validation passed
    
    ${status_report}     Set Variable    System diagnostic: 3 warnings, 1 critical error
    Should Contain       ${status_report}    critical error
    Log                  Status report validated successfully

exercises.title: Should Be True/False - Boolean Validation
exercises.description: Learn to validate boolean conditions and logical expressions.

story.setup: MENTOR-9: "Sometimes you need to evaluate conditions—is the temperature safe? Are repairs complete? Boolean assertions handle this."
story.context: Boolean validations check if conditions are True or False. Essential for conditional logic verification.
story.success: MENTOR-9: "Excellent! You verified that 5 > 3 is True. Boolean logic is the foundation of intelligent testing."

instructions: Create a test case named 'Conditional Validation'
Use Should Be True with expression: ${temp} < ${max_temp}
Use Should Be True to verify ${repairs_done}
Use Should Be False to verify ${system_offline}
hints: Should Be True syntax: Should Be True    ${condition} or ${expression}
Should Be False syntax: Should Be False    ${condition}
Expressions: ${x} > ${y}, ${x} < ${y}, ${x} == ${y}
${True} and ${False} are Robot Framework boolean constants
Expressions are evaluated as Python expressions
Use quotes for string comparisons: '${x}' == 'value'

exercises.title: Numeric Comparisons - Greater/Less Than
exercises.description: Learn to validate numeric ranges and thresholds.

story.setup: MENTOR-9: "Temperature limits, response times—numbers need range checks."
story.context: Numeric assertions verify values fall within acceptable ranges.
story.success: MENTOR-9: "Perfect! Numeric assertions prevent critical failures."

hints: Should Be Less Than: ${actual} ${max}
Should Be Greater Than: ${actual} ${min}
exercises.solution:
*** Test Cases ***
Numeric Range Validation
    ${temperature}       Set Variable    75
    ${max_safe_temp}     Set Variable    100
    Should Be Less Than  ${temperature}    ${max_safe_temp}
    Log                  Temperature within safe range
    
    ${damage_count}      Set Variable    5
    ${min_critical}      Set Variable    3
    Should Be Greater Than    ${damage_count}    ${min_critical}
    Log                  Critical threshold exceeded

exercises.title: Length Validations - Collection Size
exercises.description: Validate the size of strings, lists, and collections.

story.setup: MENTOR-9: "How many damaged systems? Length validations verify sizes."
story.success: MENTOR-9: "Excellent! 5 systems confirmed, error code correct length."

hints: Length Should Be: ${item} ${expected_length}
Should Be Empty for zero items
exercises.solution:
*** Test Cases ***
Length Validation
    @{damaged_systems}    Create List    Navigation    Power    Life Support    Communications    Sensors
    Length Should Be      ${damaged_systems}    5
    Log                   Damage count verified
    
    ${error_code}         Set Variable    ERR-2157-03-15-HULL
    Length Should Be      ${error_code}    19
    
    @{empty_repairs}      Create List
    Should Be Empty       ${empty_repairs}
    Log                   No repairs completed

exercises.title: Assertion Flexibility - Keyword Variations
exercises.description: Understand assertion keywords are case-insensitive and spacing-flexible.

story.setup: MENTOR-9: "Assertions follow the same flexibility rules as all keywords."
story.success: MENTOR-9: "See? All assertion styles work identically."

hints: Case-insensitive: Should Be Equal = should be equal
Spacing flexible
exercises.solution:
*** Test Cases ***
Assertion Flexibility
    ${value}         Set Variable    test
    Should Be Equal  ${value}    test
    should be equal  ${value}    test
    SHOULD BE EQUAL  ${value}    test
    Log              All variations work!

exercises.title: Collection Assertions - List and Dictionary
exercises.description: Validate collections with specialized assertion keywords.

story.setup: MENTOR-9: "Collections need special assertions. Does our list contain 'Navigation'?"
story.context: Collection-specific assertions verify membership and keys.
story.success: MENTOR-9: "Perfect! Navigation found, Power key exists."

instructions: Use List Should Contain Value: verify 'Navigation' exists
Use List Should Contain Value: verify 'Power' exists
Use Dictionary Should Contain Key: verify 'Navigation'
Use Dictionary Should Contain Key: verify 'Power'
hints: List Should Contain Value: ${list} ${value}
Dictionary Should Contain Key: ${dict} ${key}
exercises.solution:
*** Test Cases ***
Collection Validation
    @{systems}                       Create List    Navigation    Power    Life Support
    List Should Contain Value        ${systems}    Navigation
    List Should Contain Value        ${systems}    Power
    Log                              Systems found
    
    &{status}                        Create Dictionary    Navigation=OFFLINE    Power=CRITICAL
    Dictionary Should Contain Key    ${status}    Navigation
    Dictionary Should Contain Key    ${status}    Power
    Log                              Dictionary validated
